summary: Khakyab Dorje (1871–1922) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1885–1892) and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thayé (~1885–1899), and later taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Khammai Dhammasami (b. 1965) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford (~2000–2004). Around 2005, he became a Fellow and Trustee at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies and a professor at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University.
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk (1938–2014) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued his traditional studies under Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.

Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (1933–2023) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (~1959–1981), founded Thrangu Monastery, served as abbot of Rumtek Monastery (~1960–2023), and directed the Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981–2023).

Khenpo Appey (1927–2010) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dzongsar Monastery (1950) and under Khenpo Dragyab Lodrö. He held posts at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as head (1972–1985) and director (attested 1991) of Sakya College.

Khenpo Dazer worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under traditional teacher Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima. He served as a teacher at both the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and Dzogchen Monastery.

Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (1924–2019) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Thrangu Monastery (~1936–1959). He served as a teacher at Rumtek Monastery from 1959 and became abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra in 1978.
Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen (b. 1946) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed traditional studies under Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.

Khenpo Palden Sherab (1938–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Gochen Monastery and Riwoche Monastery. He served as chair of the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche (1920–2009) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche and Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche. He taught at Tokyo and Kyoto universities (1960–1970), founded the Nyingmapa Wishfulfilling Center (1971), and taught at the University of Virginia.

Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and under teachers including Khenpo Shenga (~1914–1927) and Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, later teaching at Men-Tsee-Khang.
Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held academic posts at Dongguk University, where he is attested in 1983 and was attested as professor emeritus in 2007.

Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909). His career included posts at Hokkaido University (~1921–1935), the University of Tokyo as professor (~1935–1946), and Chuo University.
Kim Gutschow is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who completed a PhD at Harvard University. She served as a teacher at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott (b. 1955) works in religious studies and Indology. She held a post at the University of Leeds (~1984–2012) and took up a position at Lancaster University around 2012.

Kim Plofker (b. 1964) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She studied at Haverford College and Brown University under David Pingree, and later held posts at MIT, the American Oriental Society, and Union College (~2007).

Kimberley C. Patton (b. 1958) is a religious studies scholar who completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1981–1992). She was an assistant professor at Harvard around 1990 and an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens in 1991.

Kimiaki Tanaka (b. 1955) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1983) and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, Toho Gakuin, and Keio University.

Kimmo Koskenniemi (b. 1945) is a linguist who attended Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu. He served at the University of Helsinki as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2012) and as director of the BAULT research community (attested 2015).
Kin Cheung is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Temple University under the doctoral supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).
